muse_spark_1.3/001: The strategy is perfect minimax with random-opponent exploitation. Win if possible, block loss, otherwise force draw. Among game-theoretic equals pick the move maximizing expected score vs a random opponent, which maximizes traps/forks and win-rate vs weak policies, while never sacrificing a guaranteed draw/win vs perfect play. Fast memoized search + static priority + always-legal fallback.
muse_spark_1.3/002: The strategy is perfect Tic-Tac-Toe with exploitation of mistakes. Immediate wins are taken and immediate losses are blocked. Otherwise full minimax from our perspective (1 vs -1) is solved with memoization, score 1/0/-1 with depth adjustment: fastest win, slowest loss. Among equal-value moves the most trappy move is chosen: count opponent replies that blunder from draw to loss or loss to draw/win. This keeps the draw guarantee against perfect play while maximizing win chance against imperfect play. Corners are preferred for higher trap potential. A safe fallback guarantees a legal move.
muse_spark_1.3/003: Strategy is perfect Tic-Tac-Toe with opponent-mistake exploitation. It first guarantees game-theoretic optimality via minimax: win if possible, block forced loss, otherwise draw. Among equal outcomes it prefers fastest win and slowest loss/draw to give the opponent more chances to blunder. When several moves are all optimal draws, it breaks ties by expectimax assuming the opponent plays uniformly random after that while we continue optimally, picking the move with highest expected score. This automatically selects the trickiest openings - e.g. corner as first player where only center draws for the opponent (1/8 survival vs random) instead of center where 4/8 survive - and the only drawing defense as second player. Immediate wins/blocks are taken, symmetry and memoization keep search well under 1s, with a safe first-empty fallback to never return an illegal move.
muse_spark_1.3/004: The strategy is perfect play with trap maximization. Solve TicTacToe via minimax from the perspective of `1` to move, with depth-adjusted scoring: faster wins score higher `100+empties`, slower losses score higher `-100-empties`, draws `0`. This gives optimal win/block/draw play, fastest win and slowest loss. Among equal scoring moves, count opponent blunders: for a candidate move with value `V`, evaluate all opponent replies with perfect play and sum `S-V` for replies with `S>V`. Pick the move maximizing this trap score, i.e. fewest drawing replies when drawing, most drawing/winning replies when losing. This automatically chooses corner opening as first player which has only 1 drawing reply vs 4 for center, and center/corner defense as second player. Fallback to first empty guarantees legality and <1ms time.
muse_spark_1.3/005: The strategy is perfect play with exploitative tie-breaking. It never loses: immediate wins are taken, immediate losses are blocked, and otherwise minimax (win > draw > loss, fast win / slow loss) is used assuming optimal opponent. Among moves equal under minimax it maximizes expected value against a random opponent (we play optimally, opponent plays uniformly). This automatically prefers corners as first player, center-corner responses as second player, and fork-creating moves that give the opponent the most chances to blunder. Symmetric ties are randomized. Full search on 3x3 is tiny and memoized, well under 1s, with a safe fallback to first empty to guarantee legality.
